# Step R2 of 5: reply bar and the per-message menu

If R1 left anything unfinished or red, finish that first. The "How to work" rules from R1 apply.

1. Reply bar. In compact mode, when the reader is open and the reply composer is not, a reply bar sits in the context slot above the action pill. Render it from `ReaderView.vue` with `<Teleport>` into a new `contextHost` prop (`App.vue` passes `mobileBottomBar?.contextHost` in compact mode; disabled when the prop is missing, like the existing `backHost` and `actionsHost`). It is one full-width button inside the 44px pill: the reply glyph, then the text "Reply" at 1rem in `--text-secondary`, left-aligned, with a 48px high hit area. `data-test="mobile-reply-bar"`. It runs exactly the existing reply path (`prepareReply` in `ReaderView.vue`), with the same conditions as the existing Reply button: not rendered where that button is not rendered (`browsingOnly`), disabled with the same blocked reason as its title, and it keeps the same `aria-describedby` source label. There is no reply-all and no forward.
2. Per-message menu. In compact mode each expanded message shows a More button (48×48, 24px glyph, `data-test="message-more"`, accessible name "Message actions") at the end of its sender line. It opens `MobileActionSheet` titled with the sender's name, offering: Reply (replies to that message, through the same `prepareReply` path with that message as the source, same conditions), Collapse (collapsed messages are expanded by tapping them, as today), and Copy text (copies the message's plain-text body with `navigator.clipboard.writeText`; on success the sheet closes and a polite live region announces "Copied"; if the clipboard is unavailable or rejects, the row stays and shows "Copy unavailable" as its disabled reason: never claim success that did not happen).
3. Tests:
   - Unit: reply bar rendered only in compact mode with a context host, same disabled state and reason as the Reply control, emits the same `prepareReply` payload; not rendered while the reply composer is open or in `browsingOnly`. Message menu: opens the sheet for that message, Reply targets that message, Collapse collapses it, Copy text calls the clipboard with the body and reports failure honestly (stub `navigator.clipboard`).
   - Rendered (`tests/layout/mobile-reader.rendered.test.ts`), at 412×915 and 360×800: the reply bar is inside the context pill, above the action pill with a 12px gap, full width, at least 48px high hit area; the reader's last message scrolls clear of the reply bar; `message-more` is 48×48 and inside its message; opening it shows the sheet with three rows.
4. Run the same checks as R1. Add `reader-message-sheet.png` to the screenshot test and regenerate the screenshots into `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p2-reader`. Commit (`feat(mobile): reply bar and per-message menu`) and push.

# Step R3 of 5: outcome notice as a toast

If R2 left anything unfinished or red, finish that first. The "How to work" rules from R1 apply.

After an action (for example Mark done) the app shows an outcome notice with Undo in the notice dock (`.list-dock`, `src/components/ActionNotice.vue`). In compact mode it becomes a floating toast above the bottom pills. Behaviour, wording and states do not change: the app's rule is honest state, so pending, done, failed, partial, "outcome unknown" and "Undo expired" must all stay visible and distinct, and the notice stays as long as it does today.

1. CSS only, in `notices.css`, compact mode: `.list-dock` is already positioned just above the bottom region by `shell.css` (`bottom: var(--mobile-bottom-clearance)`). Style `.action-notice` inside it as a pill: `--surface-raised` background, 1px `--divider` border, 14px radius, 12px/16px padding, a soft shadow (`--overlay-lift` is too strong; use `0 4px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`), full width minus the 16px side margins. Text at `--type-body`; the label and the status wrap onto further lines instead of truncating. The Undo button (and "Check acceptance", and the group Undo) sits at the end as a 48px high target in `--focus-accent`, weight 600. The keyboard hint (`kbd` "Z") is not shown in compact mode.
2. The empty notice (`.action-notice-empty`) takes no space and shows nothing. The command error line (`.command-error`) and the reminder confirmation get the same pill treatment with their existing tone colours.
3. The dock must never cover the bottom pills, and when the context slot is filled (split tabs or the reply bar) the toast sits above it: `--mobile-bottom-clearance` already accounts for that; verify it rather than hard-coding offsets.
4. Tests:
   - CSS contract tests for `notices.css`.
   - Rendered (`tests/layout/mobile-reader.rendered.test.ts`), at 412×915 and 360×800: in the reader, activate Mark done; the notice is visible, inside the viewport, entirely above the reply bar and the action pill (no overlap), its Undo button at least 48px high; the status text is fully visible (its scroll width does not exceed its client width); activating Undo restores the conversation. # Step R4 of 5: full-screen compose and reply

If R3 left anything unfinished or red, finish that first. The "How to work" rules from R1 apply.

Read `src/components/ComposeCard.vue`, `ReplyComposer.vue`, `DraftEditorCore.vue`, `DraftAlerts.vue` and how `App.vue` mounts them (`composeCardOpen`, `replyComposerOpen`, `releaseEditorSurface`) first. The editor's behaviour is delicate (protected close, save states, conflict and recovery alerts, IME guards): do not change any of it. This step is layout only.

1. In compact mode both editors (new message card and reply composer) present as a full-screen sheet that covers the whole `.app`, including the top bar and the bottom region (`position: absolute; inset: 0` inside `.app`, above the frame, below overlays and dialogs). CSS in `compose.css`; add a compact class or attribute on the editor roots only if CSS alone cannot target them.
   - Header row, 56px: the title ("New message" or "Reply", the existing heading text) at 1rem weight 600 on the left; on the right a round 40px close button in a 48px hit area that runs the existing protected close ("Save and close"), keeping its existing hook and accessible name.
   - Under the header, always visible, the existing status line that says the draft is saved locally and is not sent, in `--mobile-type-meta`. Do not shorten or hide it.
   - Fields: To, Cc (behind its existing toggle), Subject as full-width rows at least 48px high with a 1px `--rule` under each, label in `--text-secondary`, input text at 1rem (16px, which also prevents zoom-on-focus on phones). The body textarea fills all remaining height, 1rem, line height 1.5, no border, no resize handle, 20px/16px side insets.
   - Footer row, pinned to the bottom of the sheet above the safe area: the existing actions (Save and close, Discard…) as buttons at least 48px high; the keyboard hint (`Esc`) is not shown in compact mode. The discard confirmation and every alert (`DraftAlerts`, conflict, recovery) stay visible inside the sheet, above the footer, and wrap.
   - For a reply, the thread is not visible behind the sheet; the existing line that names what is being replied to stays at the top of the fields.
2. Software keyboard: the Android activity uses `adjustResize`, so the WebView's layout viewport shrinks when the keyboard opens. Make the sheet follow the visual viewport so the footer and the caret stay visible: size the sheet with `100dvh`-based or container-based heights (the `.app` root must not be taller than the visible area), and add a small composable that listens to `window.visualViewport` `resize`/`scroll` and keeps the focused field scrolled into view inside the sheet. Unit-test the composable with a stubbed `visualViewport`.
3. Android Back and Escape close the sheet through the existing protected close path (the Escape ladder already handles the editors: verify with a test, do not add a second path). A draft that cannot be saved must keep the sheet open with its alert, as today.
4. Tests:
   - Unit: App-level tests in compact mode that compose opens the sheet, that the status line and both footer actions are present, that Escape runs the protected close; all existing compose and reply tests pass untouched.
   - CSS contract tests for `compose.css`.
   - Rendered: new `tests/layout/mobile-compose.rendered.test.ts` (add to `test:rendered`), at 412×915 and 360×800: open compose from the top bar; the sheet covers the app (top bar and bottom region are not hit-testable: `document.elementFromPoint` at their positions returns an element inside the sheet); header, fields, body and footer are inside the viewport in that vertical order with no overlap; inputs compute to 16px font size; every button at least 48px high; the body is the tallest element; nothing overflows horizontally. Then shrink the viewport height to 500px (simulating the keyboard) and assert the footer and the header are still inside the viewport and the body is still at least 120px tall. Then open a conversation, use the reply bar, and assert the same for the reply sheet. Closing returns to the previous surface.
5. Run the same checks as R1. Update the screenshot test: `compose.png`, `compose-keyboard.png` (viewport height 500), `reply.png`; regenerate into `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p2-reader`. Commit (`feat(mobile): full-screen compose and reply`) and push.

# Review fixes after merging the list and reader tracks

Both tracks are merged into `mobile/integration` (a574927). The coordinator
reviewed screenshots of the merged tree and found the problems below. Work on
branch `mobile/p2-fixes`, created from `origin/mobile/integration`.

Protocol for every turn: take the first unticked item, implement it now, run its
check, tick it (`[x]`), add one line under it for any decision, then
`git add -A && git commit` naming the item and `git push -u origin mobile/p2-fixes`
(retry on a remote pack error). Then take the next item if the turn has room.
End the turn with one line: which items you ticked. A turn without an edit, a
commit and a push is a failure. If an item is blocked after three real attempts,
write the exact failing output under it, leave it unticked and go on.

Standing rules: no `implement` skill, no delegation, no subagents, no
`view_image`, no cargo or Android builds, regular layout unchanged, compact CSS
only in `src/assets/mobile/*.css` scoped under `.app[data-layout="compact"]`,
no `!important`, no media queries, no `any`, readable multi-line code. Fix the
layout, never weaken an assertion; where an existing assertion passed although
the screen was wrong, strengthen it as the item says.

Commands:

- Unit: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm vitest run <files>`; full: `pnpm test > /tmp/mobile-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -8 /tmp/mobile-fix-test.log`
- Rendered (one file): `EMAIL_OS_RUN_RENDERED=1 EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts <file>`

- Screenshots: `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome EMAIL_OS_SCREENSHOT_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p2-fixes mise run screenshots:mobile`

## Items

- [ ] 1. Screenshot test (`tests/layout/mobile-screenshots.rendered.test.ts`) on the merged tree: the case "captures the list surfaces" fails with "Timed out waiting for reader archive action", and `reply.png` and `search.png` were captured at a 500px high viewport because an earlier case left the viewport shrunk. Make every `it` set the 412×915 phone viewport at its start, make the `compose-keyboard.png` step restore the viewport afterwards, and fix the failing wait (in compact mode the reader's Mark done button is `[data-test="reader-archive-toggle"]` inside `[data-test="mobile-reader-actions"]`). Check: the screenshots command passes all cases and writes every file.
- [ ] 2. Reply editor is not full-screen. In `reply.png` the reply composer is docked inside the reader: the top bar's Back button overlaps the "Reply draft" header, the reader's messages and the action pill are still visible below it. Required (step R4): in compact mode the reply composer is a sheet covering the whole `.app` (`position: absolute; inset: 0`, above the top bar and the bottom region), header row with the title on the left and the round close button on the right, status line, fields, body filling the remaining height, footer pinned at the bottom. If the composer is mounted inside the reader pane, whose overflow or stacking context clips it, move its mount point in compact mode (Teleport to the `.app` root) rather than fighting the clip in CSS. Strengthen `tests/layout/mobile-compose.rendered.test.ts` for the reply sheet at both sizes: its box equals the app's box (±1px); `document.elementFromPoint` at the centre of where the top bar's Back button, the reply bar and the action pill were returns an element inside the sheet; the reader's message text is not hit-testable; the body textarea is at least 200px tall at 915px height. Check: that rendered file passes and `pnpm vitest run tests/drafts tests/reader tests/layout` is green.
- [ ] 3. New-message editor does not cover the top bar. In `compose.png` the menu and compose buttons are still visible above the sheet's header. Same requirement as item 2: the sheet's box equals the app's box, the top bar is not hit-testable. Header layout for both editors: title at the start (left), close button at the end (right). Strengthen the rendered assertions the same way (elementFromPoint at the menu button and the compose button returns an element inside the sheet; title's left edge is left of the close button's left edge). Check: that rendered file passes.
- [ ] 4. Focused row has no date. In `inbox.png` the first row (the list's keyboard-cursor row) shows the attachment glyph but no date; every other row shows one. In compact mode `.row-time` must be displayed on every row whatever its focus, hover or selection state, and the regular layout's swap of the date for row actions must not apply. Find the rule in `src/assets/style.css` that hides the time (search for `.row-time` and `.focused`, `:hover`, `:focus-within`, `.actions-open`) and override it in `list.css`. Strengthen `tests/layout/mobile-list.rendered.test.ts`: for **each** of the first five rows, with the first row focused (`element.focus()`), `.row-time` has a non-zero box, `visibility: visible`, and non-empty text. Check: that rendered file passes.

Required: in selection mode (`.inbox-list.selecting`) each row's content is indented so that a 48px wide start gutter holds the checkbox: a 20px visual box centred in a 48×48 hit area, with no outline or border drawn around the hit area itself; the unread dot is not shown while selecting. Find what reserves the extra height in `.list-dock` in compact mode (the regular layout reserves a 36px line and other dock children may keep height while empty) and remove it for compact. Rendered assertion for that gap at both sizes. Check: `tests/layout/mobile-list.rendered.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] 7. Toast keyboard hint: in `reader-undo-toast.png` the toast still shows the "Z" key cap next to Undo. Key caps (`kbd`) inside the notice dock are not displayed in compact mode. Rendered assertion in `tests/layout/mobile-reader.rendered.test.ts`: no `kbd` inside `.list-dock` has a non-zero box. Check: that rendered file passes.
- [ ] 8. Full `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, full rendered suite, screenshots. # Mobile P3, pages track

You are implementing the remaining surfaces of a phone layout for Email OS (Tauri 2 + Vue 3 + TypeScript). A coordinator (another agent) reviews your work, does all visual review and all Android builds, and merges. The work is a checklist of 15 small items; you do one or two items per turn.

## Setup (first thing this turn)

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in this fresh worktree (branch `mobile/p3-pages`, created from `origin/mobile/integration`).

## The checklist

`/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p3-pages/PROGRESS.md`. Read it now and follow its protocol exactly: take the first unticked item, implement it immediately, run its check, tick it, commit, push, then take the next one if the turn has room. Each item states what to build, how to verify it and which files are involved.

A turn that only reads files, or that ends with "not complete" without an edit, a commit and a push, is a failure. Do not stop at the first obstacle: read the failing output, inspect the DOM or computed styles in the rendered harness, and fix the cause.

## Rules

- Implement everything yourself in this worktree. Do **not** use the repository's `implement` skill, do not delegate, do not start subagents.
- Do **not** call `view_image` or open any image file; the coordinator reviews screenshots. You verify with unit tests and geometry assertions in rendered tests.
- Do **not** run `cargo`, `mise run check:all` or `mise run android:build`. No Rust, no Kotlin.
- UI only, over features the app already has. No IPC or engine changes. Out of scope, with no placeholders: calendar, AI, voice, send, HTML bodies, label chips, multiple splits, trash/spam/move actions, reply-all, forward.
- The regular (desktop) layout must not change. Everything is compact-only markup (`layoutMode === 'compact'` in `App.vue`, or a `compact` prop) or CSS scoped under `.app[data-layout="compact"]` in `src/assets/mobile/`. No `!important`, no media queries.
- Code style: match the codebase. One CSS declaration per line, one selector per line; Vue templates one element per line with wrapped attributes (see `src/components/mobile/MobileDrawer.vue`); no `any`; tests as readable multi-line code. Project tokens and glyph components only; no text or emoji characters as icons. Wording is terse and factual (`PRODUCT.md`).
- Touch targets at least 48×48 CSS px; keep accessible names, keyboard focus and `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour; existing `data-test` hooks keep their names.

## What exists on your base branch

- `src/composables/useLayoutMode.ts` (`compact` below 720px); `App.vue` sets `data-layout` on `.app`.
- `src/components/mobile/`: `MobileTopBar.vue`, `MobileBottomBar.vue` (navigation pill, Account button, reader actions host, context slot), `MobileDrawer.vue` (navigation drawer, rows from `availableActions`), `MobileActionSheet.vue` (generic bottom sheet; the reader's More sheet and the per-message sheet use it).
- `src/assets/mobile/`: `tokens.css` (including `--mobile-bottom-clearance`), `shell.css`, `list.css`, `drawer.css`, `reader.css`, `sheet.css`, `notices.css`, `compose.css`. List them through `mobileCssFiles` in `tests/support/css-contract.ts`.
- `InboxList.vue` has a `compact` prop with swipe actions (`src/composables/useSwipeAction.ts`) and long-press selection.
- Rendered harness `tests/rendered/chromium.ts` with `PHONE_VIEWPORT`; existing phone tests in `tests/layout/mobile-*.rendered.test.ts` (read one for the conventions: the preview mounts two workspaces, always query inside `.workspace-panel:not([inert]) .app`). Screenshots: `tests/layout/mobile-screenshots.rendered.test.ts`.
- Contract and design: `docs/ux-14-mobile-shell.md`, `DESIGN.md` "Compact layout (phone)".
- Another thread is fixing review findings in `list.css`, `compose.css`, `InboxList.vue`, the editors and the screenshot test on branch `mobile/p2-fixes`. Avoid those files except where an item requires it, and keep edits to `App.vue` small and local.

This turn: setup, then items 1 and 2. Your first tool calls after reading PROGRESS.md should be commands and edits. Do not end the turn before item 1 is ticked, committed and pushed.

Draft while the last polish round lands. Do not merge yet.

## What this is

A phone layout for the Android fixture build, over features the app already has. The desktop layout is unchanged: everything is compact-only markup or CSS scoped under `.app[data-layout="compact"]` in `src/assets/mobile/`, switched by viewport width (`useLayoutMode`, below 720px).

- **Frame:** top bar, bottom navigation, dark system bars, Android Back following the Escape ladder.
- **List:** stacked rows, split tabs in a floating pill, navigation drawer, swipe to mark done or remind (with Undo), long-press selection.
- **Reader:** bottom action bar (star, remind, done, previous, next, more), action sheets, reply bar, per-message menu, outcome toast.
- **Editors:** full-screen new message and reply, usable above the software keyboard. Drafts stay local; there is no send path.
- **Other surfaces:** search, reminders and the reminder picker, drafts, activity, command palette, contact details, settings with swipe preferences.

Scope decisions are in `docs/adr/0003-mobile-layout.md`; behaviour is in `docs/ux-14-mobile-shell.md`.

## Not included

Send, HTML message bodies, label chips, multiple splits, trash/spam/move actions, reply-all, forward, calendar, AI and voice. Gmail on Android is not part of this; the Android build runs on fixture data.

## Validation

Filled in when the polish round is merged: unit and rendered counts, CI, and the emulator pass.
